title: SCIM termination handshake: tenant quarantine window, idempotent retries, and DLQ safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: customer-facing incidents show premature user deletion during SCIM deprovision flows when downstream systems are temporarily unavailable. This leads to orphaned session tokens, missing group memberships, and difficult recovery workflows for enterprise customers. Scope: users + group membership sync via SCIM (customer IdP -> Redwood SCIM endpoint). Goals: 1) Add a termination handshake with configurable quarantine TTL per-tenant that delays irreversible cleanup for N minutes; 2) Implement idempotent retry semantics and exponential backoff + jitter on the provisioner with a bounded DLQ to prevent silent data loss; 3) Surface observability for retry storms and quarantined objects and add admin controls to force-complete or abort quarantine; 4) Ensure audit logs record every state transition with actor metadata for compliance.
tasks: Design: termination handshake state machine and tenant-level quarantine TTL (product & security signoff)
Runtime: add quarantine state to SCIM user/group model and tombstone metadata (actor, ts, source-change-id)
API: extend SCIM response codes to return 202 + X-Quarantine-Until for soft-delete acknowledgement
Retries: implement exponential backoff with full jitter and per-tenant circuit-breaker thresholds
DLQ: route unresolvable operations to a tenant-scoped DLQ with metadata and automatic retry/backoff policy
Idempotency: create reconciliation tokens (change_id) and de-dup logic in workers
Observability: dashboards (counters, 99th latency, retry-per-minute, DLQ size), tracing spans for handshake transitions
Admin UI: console controls for tenant admins to view quarantined objects and force-commit or restore
Tests: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests against a SCIM stub, chaos tests where downstream returns 503/timeout
Rollout: canary to 10% of tenants, monitor error budget and DLQ growth, then progressive ramp
acceptance_criteria: SCIM soft-delete returns 202 and includes X-Quarantine-Until header when TTL > 0
Quarantined objects visible in console with age, source-change-id and actor fields
Retry worker performs idempotent retries using change_id; duplicate requests do not create duplicate users or groups
DLQ entries include original request payload, error reason, and tenant id; DLQ size exposed in metrics
Chaos test with simulated downstream 503 results in quarantined objects and no irreversible deletions
Security/compliance signoff recorded in Confluence and audit logs include granular state transitions
notes: Design trade-offs: keeping a TTL reduces immediate data deletion risk but increases reconciliation complexity (tombstone growth). We limit default TTL to 30 minutes and allow enterprise tenants to configure up to 7 days.
We considered synchronous retries in the API path but chose async worker retries to avoid holding IdP connections and to support exponential backoff with host-level circuit breakers.

Idempotency approach: prefer source-supplied change_id when available (Okta/G Suite provide structured events). If missing, create a deterministic hash of (tenant, scim_op, payload) and store as change_id for 72 hours.
DLQ policy: automatic re-attempt every hour for 24 hours, then require manual review; escalations surface to oncall if DLQ growth > 1000 entries for any tenant.
Admin controls: console action triggers a signed admin operation that is written to the audit log and emits a tracing span tagged with admin user id and action reason.
Privacy: tombstones store minimal PII (external_id, tenancy, object_type, change_id) and avoid storing raw credentials or tokens.
Operational runbook stub: steps to reconcile when identities are desynced, how to reconstruct group memberships from audit trail and evaluation checklist for forced purge.
Edge-case: overlapping group and user changes (remove from group + delete user) should respect ordering from change_id timestamps; reconciliation worker enforces causal ordering when possible.
